decisions: The cap comes from one formula with no level gate: `Math.max(ECONOMY.interestCap, contentSetTune('checkout', level).interestCap)`. ECONOMY holds the base values (`interestPer: 10`, `interestCap: 3`), and the Checkout tune holds `interestCap: [0, 6, 10]`. The L1 value of 0 means the base cap applies, so levels 0 and 1 give 3, L2 gives 6 and L3 gives 10, and no number appears twice. Why: a content file cannot import ECONOMY, because data/waves imports data/enemies, which imports engine/registry, which eagerly globs content/sets/*, and that is an import cycle. A side effect of max semantics is that if a later unit raises the base cap above 6, Checkout L2 stops doing anything. The literal-number tests would catch that.

`interestPer` was removed from the Checkout tune, and the set text no longer uses `{interestPer}`, for the same import-cycle reason. The L2 text is now 'Interest cap raised to {interestCap}' and the L3 text is 'Shop prices −X%; interest cap raised to {interestCap}'. The German versions are 'Zinsobergrenze steigt auf {interestCap}' and 'Shop-Preise −X %; Zinsobergrenze steigt auf {interestCap}'.

decisions: Shared ★3 text mechanism. The ranged unit had already committed one (ItemText.star3, which itemRules appends from ★3 on, validated in registry.ts). I cherry-picked its commit 9005794 unchanged as b9675b1 instead of writing my own, so both branches carry an identical diff. A trial merge of the integration tip 2b0b851 plus both star-3 branches merged cleanly, with tsc clean and 2277 of 2277 tests passing. As in that commit, the content text carries its own '★3: ' prefix.

Tier gate. I added hasStar3(tier) to define.ts, an additive one-line export. Every ★3 number is a scalar tune key: fullArc, slamStun, pullIn, lifeMult, freeze and pickupMult. A per-tier [0,0,x] array would extrapolate to 2x at ★4, because tuneValue continues the last step. The ranged unit uses [0,0,1] flag triples instead, and the cherry-picked itemRules uses a literal `tier >= 3`. The integrator can unify the two styles.

Frying Pan. The gate sits in sweep.ts: at ★3 the half-arc comes from tune.fullArc (360) instead of st.arcDeg. A base-phase build hook would have changed the arcDeg stat, Duct Tape's tapeArc snapshot (synergies.ts:62) and build.json. At ★3 the swoosh sprite spins a full turn, so hits behind the cart have a visual. ctx.sweep (Express Checkout) gets the full arc too.

Spray Bottle. The suggested soak already happens at every tier (spray.ts tune.wet, pinned by tests/wet.test.ts), so ★3 does something else. The spray's own 'pattern:cone' hook destroys enemy shots inside the cone, using ctx.enemyShots and killShot (the path Smoothie Shield uses). No combo gives the spray this. The hook checks ev.stats.type === spray, so the Leaf Blower on the same pattern is unaffected. Nothing in this behavior needs a tune number.

Leaf Blower. Walls and props are tracked in the scene (enemies.ts:273 calls slamEnemy), so I built the primary behavior, not the fallback. cone.ts sets a new optional HitOpts.blowStun (hooks.ts) from tune.slamStun at ★3. ArenaScene keeps it as e.blownStun next to the blow mark and calls stunEnemy after the slam damage. slideEnemy resets it to 0, so an Ice Sheet slide never inherits a stun. The stun is untagged, so stunEnemy keeps bosses immune.

Blender. At ★3 the per-tick knockback of 20 points inward instead of outward. Enemies closer than player.radius + enemy.radius + 12 (the Vacuum's nozzle distance) are still pushed out, so the pull never feeds melee enemies into the goblin. The change is in aura.ts and reads tune.pullIn.

Mop. dropPuddle in puddle.ts multiplies st.duration by tune.lifeMult (2) at ★3. st.duration already includes the Cleaning set's +1/+2 s, so that bonus doubles too: (3+2)x2 = 10 s at Cleaning level 3, pinned in mop.test.ts. The Snow Cone has no lifeMult key and keeps 4 s, which is also tested.

Snow Cone. Its own 'pattern:puddleEnter' hook works like Black Ice and calls ctx.stun(enemy, 0.5, frost) when `first` is set. It checks ev.stats.type === snowcone, because c.touches would also match the puddles of a Mop placed next to it (tested). No PatternScene change was needed. A test confirms the freeze never sets off Ice Sheet, because the stun runs outside a hit and a frozen enemy cannot slide. That keeps the rules text ('from another source') true.

Vacuum. At ★3 the whole pickup radius doubles all the time, not only 'while it pulses'. The radius is a build stat with no runtime modifier (ArenaScene.updateCoins reads store.state.build.pickupRadius every frame), the bot reads the same build value, and in a fight the vacuum pulses whenever an enemy is in range. The doubling sits in its existing final-phase player hook, moved to order 10 so it runs after Magnet. It doubles base, +60, Magnet and the perk together.

Vacuum utility framing. The blurb now reads 'Utility weapon. Sucks groceries closer, and coins too.' in EN and 'Hilfswaffe. Saugt Gegner heran, Münzen übrigens auch.' in DE. I did not add a 'utility' WeaponTag or kind label, which would touch types, KIND_BY_TAG, CSS and i18n. ★1 and ★2 rules text is unchanged for all seven weapons.
Numbers. The spec gave none, so I picked them: slamStun 0.5 s, freeze 0.5 s (Black Ice uses 0.8), pullIn 20 (the same size as the old outward push), lifeMult 2, pickupMult 2, fullArc 360.
Sim notes. The seven weapon-<id> sims place each weapon at ★3, so I updated their notes to describe the new behavior, as the ranged unit did for its six.

Shared files. Every edit to a shared file is additive: define.ts (hasStar3, plus ItemText.star3 from the cherry-pick), hooks.ts (HitOpts.blowStun), scenes/enemies.ts (Enemy.blownStun), ArenaScene.ts (three lines), and from the cherry-pick registry.ts and i18n/data.ts. I did not touch pulse.ts, types.ts, common.ts, fakeHost.ts or ctx.ts.

Test discipline. On a scratch worktree at a405b5d with my test files checked out, every new test fails and every existing test I only moved to ★2 still passes. I folded the two same-pattern negative controls (the Blower does not wash, the Spray carries no stun) into the positive tests so that each test fails on base.

It ran sim weapon-leafblower with the 8 dummies moved against the right wall. The unit tests only cover the handoff (opts.blowStun at ★2, ★3 and ★4) plus source guards. In that setup the stun uptime is high (inferred: about 22 x 0.5 s spread over 8 enemies in 6 s). Vacuum ★3 as specced has almost no mechanical value. updateCoins removes a coin only when it is collected, so coins never expire. The end of an aisle pulls in every coin. The build lab awards coins without any pickup radius, so it measures zero as well. Whether to keep this ★3 or pick another is a product call for the parent.
The Snow Cone freeze does count in the build lab, because a foe in the 'stun' state skips moving and attacking (src/buildlab/combat.ts:330).

Frying Pan side effects. On a ★3 Pan, Duct Tape's +60° arc does nothing (the sweep is already 360°), but describeBuffs still shows the tape line. Sizzling Skillet still spreads its pools over the 150° front arc, because it reads st.arcDeg.
There are now two ★3 gate styles: hasStar3 with scalar tune keys in this unit, [0,0,1] flag triples in the ranged unit, and a literal `tier >= 3` in itemRules. Unifying them is up to the integrator.
